# GitFi.fun

> GitFi is the market layer for open source. It turns a public GitHub repository into one verified on-chain market on NEAR, with wallet-signed trading, creator royalties, platform fees and staker yield.

## Canonical links

- App: https://gitfi.fun
- Docs: https://docs.gitfi.fun
- Docs mirror: https://gitfi.fun/docs/
- Market contract: https://explorer.testnet.near.org/accounts/market.gitfi-395012.testnet
- Repo registry: https://explorer.testnet.near.org/accounts/registry.gitfi-395012.testnet

## What GitFi does

1. A builder connects a NEAR wallet with NEP-413. No GitHub OAuth is used.
2. The builder proves ownership by adding one sync line to the public README.
3. The builder pays a 1 NEAR platform launch fee.
4. The verified repository gets exactly one token and one market on NEAR.
5. The launch market cap is $10,000 + $10 per GitHub star. The server converts that cap to a real NEAR launch price with the live NEAR/USD quote.
6. Users buy and sell with NEAR. Balances, cost basis and every trade are recorded by the market contract.
7. The creator earns 0.5% of every trade, the platform earns 0.3%, and token stakers earn 0.5%. Total trade fee: 1.3%.

## Ownership rule

Only the README-verified repository owner can create the token/market. One repository can have exactly one token. A second wallet cannot launch a market from someone else's repository.

## What is real

- NEAR testnet contracts are deployed and public.
- Buy/sell, staking, reward claims and bounties are wallet-signed on-chain actions.
- Home, Explore, Portfolio and Leaderboard read the market contract; market prices are displayed in USD using a live NEAR/USD quote while settlement is in NEAR.
- There is no demo faucet, demo USDC trading path, or sandbox wallet login in the UI.

## Current testnet scope

- The market is a step-price market with an on-chain reserve, not a full constant-product DEX.
- Tokens currently use an internal ledger inside the market contract, not a standalone NEP-141 contract per repository.
- The old seeded testnet markets were removed; the active market set is intentionally clean and owner-gated.
- Mainnet requires fresh contracts, production owner/treasury accounts, a clean database, and an external security audit.

## For hackathon judges

Start at https://docs.gitfi.fun/#judges for the five-minute tour: thesis, mechanism, why NEAR is load-bearing, and an honest list of what is still mainnet work.

## Status

Testnet build. Not audited. Contracts and docs are the source of truth.
